title: U.S. House · New York's 2nd Congressional District
area: West-central Suffolk County on Long Island, including Babylon, Islip, and parts of Smithtown.

context.text: Both parties' primaries were canceled; incumbent Andrew Garbarino advanced unopposed on the Republican and Conservative lines, and Patrick Halpin advanced unopposed on the Democratic and Working Families Party lines after four other Democrats withdrew. As of September 22, 2026, Cook Political Report and Inside Elections rated the general election "Solid Republican," Decision Desk rated it "Likely Republican," and Sabato's Crystal Ball rated it "Safe Republican."

summary.text: Andrew Garbarino is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for New York's 2nd Congressional District. A Long Island native and attorney, he served in the New York State Assembly from 2013 to 2020 before being elected to Congress in 2020. He chairs the House Homeland Security Committee and also serves on the Financial Services and Ethics committees.

background.text: Born in Sayville, New York, in 1984, and raised there; graduated from Sayville High School.
Earned a B.A. in history and classical humanities from George Washington University and a J.D. from Hofstra University.
Worked at his family's law firm in Sayville after law school.
Represented the 7th District in the New York State Assembly from 2013 to 2020, winning the seat in 2012 and re-election in 2014, 2016 and 2018.

In the Assembly, according to his campaign website's text republished by Ballotpedia, he voted against the 2019 bail-reform bill and cosponsored a bill making it a felony to intentionally interfere with a police or peace officer performing official duties.

Won the 2020 Republican primary for NY-2 after Rep. Peter King announced his retirement, then defeated Democrat Jackie Gordon in the general election; he took office January 3, 2021 and was re-elected in 2022 and 2024.

Committee assignments for the 119th Congress are Homeland Security (Chairman), Financial Services (Vice Chairman of the Capital Markets Subcommittee) and Ethics. He became Homeland Security chair in July 2025 after the resignation of Mark Green.

His House biography says he co-chairs the Congressional SALT Caucus and led negotiations to raise the State and Local Tax deduction cap to $40,000, and that he has worked on funding for the World Trade Center Health Program.
Member of the Sayville Rotary Club and Knights of Columbus; his official biography describes him as a lifelong Long Islander.

priorities.text: Campaign material lists support for law enforcement, combating the opioid epidemic, supporting veterans, and protecting the Great South Bay and Long Island's environment as priorities.

positions.summary: Opposes efforts to defund the police and says he has "wholeheartedly backed New York's finest"; endorsed by multiple law-enforcement unions.
positions.quote: Andrew has opposed all efforts to defund the police.

record.text: Serves on the House Homeland Security Committee (Chairman, Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Subcommittee) and House Financial Services Committee (Vice Chair) in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

As a New York State Assemblyman, voted against the 2019 state bail-reform legislation and voted for bills mandating insurance coverage of opioid-overdose reversal medication (NARCAN/Naloxone) and shortening opioid prescriptions to 7 days.

summary.text: Patrick Halpin is the Democratic and Working Families Party nominee in NY-2. A former Suffolk County legislator, New York State Assemblyman and Suffolk County Executive, he later chaired the Suffolk County Water Authority. His campaign says he is running on affordability, public safety, housing and protecting drinking water.

background.text: Born in 1953 and grew up on Long Island's South Shore; he was student body president at West Babylon High School, according to his campaign website.
Earned a B.A. in political science and economics from Old Dominion University, according to Wikipedia; he then worked as a campaign staffer and congressional aide for U.S. Rep. Tom Downey.
First elected to public office at age 26, representing the 13th District of the Suffolk County Legislature starting in 1979.
Served in the New York State Assembly from 1982 to 1987; he was the first Democrat elected to the Assembly from the Town of Babylon area in over a century, according to his campaign website.

Elected Suffolk County Executive in 1987 at age 34, the youngest in county history, and served one term. He says he created the Long Island Housing Partnership and launched community-based policing and anti-domestic-violence programs.

Worked as Executive Vice President of the Institute for Student Achievement from 1994 and later as a managing director of Mercury Public Affairs, according to Wikipedia; his campaign says he hosted public-affairs television programs.
Joined the Suffolk County Water Authority board in 2006 and became its chairman in December 2018.
According to his campaign website, he chaired the Town of Babylon Industrial Development Agency and currently chairs the Town of Babylon Planning Board.

priorities.text: Says his campaign centers on affordability (housing, groceries, childcare), health care access and cost, and public safety paired with "sensible immigration" reform.
priorities.quote: It shouldn't be this hard to build a life on Long Island.

priorities.text: Names health care, the environment, Social Security, and reducing corruption in Washington as the public-policy areas he is most passionate about.

positions.summary: Says health care access should not depend on ZIP code, job, or bank account, and criticizes his opponent's vote that he says will cause New Yorkers to lose Medicaid coverage.
positions.quote: Healthcare shouldn't depend on your ZIP code, your job, or your bank account.

record.text: As Suffolk County Executive, says he created the Long Island Housing Partnership and negotiated a county police contract while chairing efforts on community policing and domestic-violence protections.

researchNotes: Garbarino has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey in 2020, 2022, 2024, or 2026; his priorities and record here draw on his campaign website text as republished by Ballotpedia. This is a low-competitiveness race (rated Solid/Safe Republican), so depth is limited per the BASIC research tier. Halpin's pre-1994 career dates come from Wikipedia and his campaign site; no official biography was found for him.
